findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the web request path
findings.body: Translations load lazily, and `translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. Fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` here in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks and any code that sets `I18n.locale` or uses `I18n.with_locale` outside a controller never load them. A missing key there will not fall back to the site default or English, so the user gets 'translation missing' output. This is most likely in emails sent in a user's locale. Loading the fallback locales should happen inside the I18n layer (e.g. in `translate`/`load_locale`), not only in a controller filter.

findings.title: Fallback list reads SiteSetting (DB-backed) on every lookup and can fail or return stale results
findings.body: `Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on each translation, so `SiteSetting.default_locale` runs on every lookup. Early in boot, during migrations or asset precompile, or before the settings table exists, `SiteSetting` may not be usable. If `default_locale` returns nil, `.to_sym` raises NoMethodError before `.compact` can help, and the `.compact` is useless where it sits. The translate accelerator's LRU cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`, which ignores the site default locale. A cached fallback-resolved string can therefore stay stale after an admin changes the default locale. Guard against a nil or unavailable setting and include the fallback chain in the cache key, or clear the cache when the setting changes.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! initializes and checks @loaded_locales outside the mutex
findings.body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` and the `include?` check run without `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `reload!` reassigns `@loaded_locales = []` and `load_locale` mutates it under the mutex. Concurrent requests can race on the unsynchronized initialization or read. A fully safe approach would take the lock, or simply delegate to `load_locale`, which already rechecks under the lock.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: The PR replaces the Rails `config.i18n.fallbacks` setting with a custom fallback list, lazy loading of fallback locales, and a new `ensure_loaded!` method. It adds no specs. Nothing covers the fallback order (user, site default, en), a missing key falling back correctly, or the interaction with the lazy locale loader and LRU cache. A regression in any of these would not be caught.
